title: Supplementary Online Information for Cooper et al. (2026)
text:
This site provides supplementary information to help enable reproduction and independent exploration of the statistical analyses reported in Cooper et al. (2026).
The pages in the Analyses section describe regression modelling for the manuscript “Structural and functional basis of lipid-associated, electrogenic ammonium transport by the Rhesus-family protein NeRh50 in Nitrosomonas europaea” by Cooper et al. We analyse this data to establish evidence in support of answers to the following key questions:

Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to changes in lipid-protein ratio (LPR)?
Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to a change in substrate from NH4+ to MeA?
Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to a changes in pH conditions?

title: Figure 4c: WT NeRh50 maximum amplitudes and decay rate constants in response to changes in lipid-protein ratio (LPR)
text:
The Models
We use linear models for amplitude and decay rate as dependent variables, with LPR as the independent factor, checking fit in Figure 1.

Show the code
# Fit the models
model4c_amp_lm <- lm(amplitude ~ LPR, data=dfms$dfm_4c)
model4c_k_lm <- lm(decayrate ~ LPR, data=dfms$dfm_4c)

# Check model fit
performance::check_model(model4c_amp_lm)
performance::check_model(model4c_k_lm)












(a) amplitude ~ LPR











(b) decayrate ~ LPR







Figure 1: Diagnostic plots for linear model fits of amplitude ~ LPR and decayrate ~ LPR. The splines for linearity/heteroscadicity are odd, but the datapoints are not concerning. There is some evidence of non-normality of residuals in the decay rate data, but nothing especially concerning.



As the model fit is acceptable, we estimate contrasts in Table 2.


Show the code
EMM <- emmeans::emmeans(model4c_amp_lm, ~ LPR)
confint(emmeans::contrast(EMM, "pairwise", adjust="sidak")) |>
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=3) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("hover", "responsive")
  )
EMM <- emmeans::emmeans(model4c_k_lm, ~ LPR)
confint(emmeans::contrast(EMM, "pairwise", adjust="sidak")) |>
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=3) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("hover", "responsive")
  )

title: Figure 4c: WT NeRh50 maximum amplitudes and decay rate constants in response to changes in lipid-protein ratio (LPR)
text:
The Figures
We plot the differences, indicating P-values for the contrasts in Figure 2.

Show the code
# Get p-values, accounting for heteroscedasticity and multiple testing
# Also generate group1 and group2 columns
EMM_amp <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model4c_amp_lm, ~ LPR),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=2.5) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

EMM_k <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model4c_k_lm, ~ LPR),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=85) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

p4c_amp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfms$dfm_4c, 
                           ggplot2::aes(x=LPR, y=amplitude, color=LPR)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Maximum amplitude (nA)") +
  ggplot2::ylim(0, 3.5) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_amp,
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}",
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

p4c_k <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfms$dfm_4c, 
                         ggplot2::aes(x=LPR, y=decayrate, color=LPR)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Decay rate constant k (/s)") +
  ggplot2::ylim(0, 105) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_k, 
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}", 
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)
